meta.label: Electric toothbrushes
tradeoffLabels: ADA-reviewed for safety and plaque removal
meta.attribution: The ADA Seal of Acceptance is a voluntary US programme: a manufacturer submits its own test data and the ADA's Council on Scientific Affairs decides whether it shows the product is safe and effective at removing plaque and reducing gingivitis when used as directed. A brush that does not appear in the ADA's product-search tool has not necessarily failed anything; it may simply not have applied, especially if the brand sells mainly outside the US. Where a search turned up no result for a brand, the note says so and gives the date checked, rather than treating the absence as a safety finding. Where the note also cites the US Consumer Product Safety Commission's saferproducts.gov recall database, that is a separate, government-run check of whether that brand name has any recall on file, most relevant to battery and charger hazards; the CPSC's own database shows an April 2026 recall of the delivery boxes of autobrush's children's Sonic Pro Kids model (the children's model is not scored on this page; the maker's adult brush is, and the recall is reflected in its health and maker-accountability scores) for a lithium coin battery that small children could reach, which is the kind of hazard this check is meant to catch. Price here is the toothbrush handle's own listed price on the date shown, not the ongoing cost of replacement heads, which varies by brand, subscription plan and how often a head is changed, and is not scored here. Two models from the same maker (Oral-B iO against Oral-B Pro 1000, quip's rechargeable against its AAA-battery model) are scored separately because their prices and designs differ and the ADA treats them differently. ADA records change: in October 2026 the records this page had cited for Philips Sonicare ProtectiveClean, quip's rechargeable brush, Goby and Bitvae no longer resolved and did not turn up in the ADA's search, so those brushes are now scored as not listed. Where a handle price comes from a retailer rather than the maker, it is Target's listed US price on the date shown. Battery and head waste is scored only where a listing or programme states the battery type, whether it can be removed or whether the brush can be recycled; it is left blank otherwise. Not medical advice; the ADA's own guidance is that either a manual or a powered brush works when used for two minutes, twice a day, with gentle pressure. Reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: ADA Seal record and CPSC recall check
Ease of purchase and replacement heads

products.name: Manual toothbrush (skip going electric)

economical.note: The ADA's own toothbrush page states powered toothbrushes 'can be more expensive than most manual toothbrushes.'

health.note: The ADA's toothbrush page states 'both manual and powered toothbrushes are effective at removing plaque,' with powered brushes offering a practical advantage mainly for people with reduced dexterity, such as some elderly users, people with disabilities, or people wearing braces.

accessibility.note: A manual toothbrush is sold everywhere a toothbrush is sold, with no charger, no app, and no proprietary replacement head to reorder.

products.description: The ADA's own guidance says manual and powered toothbrushes remove plaque equally well when used correctly for two minutes twice a day; a basic manual toothbrush needs no charging, no subscription and no replacement head to order.

products.name: Oral-B iO Series

economical.note: Oral-B's own site prices the iO Series 4 (Matte White) at $99.99.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Oral-B' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Oral-B iO Series', applicant Procter & Gamble Co., states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed.

accessibility.note: Widely sold through major US retail, but the iO line uses its own head design rather than the round heads shared across most other Oral-B lines, and its $99.99 handle price is the second-highest in this roster.

products.description: Procter & Gamble's premium rotating-oscillating-pulsating line, individually named in its own ADA Seal record, with app-based coaching and a price well above most of this roster.

products.name: Oral-B Pro 1000

economical.note: Oral-B's own site prices the Pro 1000 rechargeable toothbrush at $49.99.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Oral-B' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for Oral-B Oscillating-Rotating-Pulsating, applicant Procter & Gamble Co., covers the Pro series (which includes Pro 1000) along with the Genius and Smart series, and states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed.

accessibility.note: One of the most widely stocked electric toothbrushes in US grocery, pharmacy and big-box retail, with round replacement heads shared across most Oral-B lines except iO.

products.description: A basic Oral-B rotating-oscillating brush covered by the same ADA Seal record as Oral-B's Pro, Genius and Smart lines, at about half the price of the iO line.

products.name: Philips Sonicare ProtectiveClean 4100

economical.note: Target's listing shows the Philips Sonicare 4100 Plaque Control at $39.99, marked down from a regular price of $49.99.

health.note: The ADA record for Philips Sonicare ProtectiveClean that this page previously cited no longer resolves (the link loops back on itself), and in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search a search for ProtectiveClean returned nothing and a search for Sonicare returned only the Philips Sonicare Power Flosser, a water flosser. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Sonicare' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Widely stocked at major US retailers such as Target and Walmart, with one cleaning mode and a pressure sensor as its main features.

products.description: Philips' entry sonic model, with a single cleaning mode and a pressure sensor; the ADA record this page once cited for the ProtectiveClean line no longer turns up in the ADA's product search (checked 2026-10).

products.name: quip Smart Rechargeable

economical.note: quip's own site lists the Smart Rechargeable Sonic Toothbrush at $55.

health.note: The ADA record for quip Electric Toothbrush - Rechargeable that this page previously cited no longer resolves (the link loops back on itself), and a search for quip in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search returned the battery model, a kids' brush, the quip 360 Oscillating Toothbrush and a toothpaste, but no rechargeable sonic model. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database showed no quip toothbrush among the records its 'quip' search returned on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through quip's own site, built around a recurring replacement-head plan rather than one-off retail purchase.

products.description: quip's rechargeable sonic brush, built around a subscription refill-head plan; unlike quip's battery model it no longer turns up in the ADA's product search (checked 2026-10).

products.name: quip Metal (AAA battery)

economical.note: quip's own site lists the Twilight Metal Sonic Toothbrush, its AAA-battery model, at $35.

health.note: The ADA's product-search record for 'quip Electric Toothbrush - Non-Rechargeable' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed. This is a separate ADA record from quip's rechargeable model.

environment.note: quip's own product page describes this model as running on a single removable AAA battery lasting over 3 months rather than a built-in rechargeable pack, so there is no sealed battery to eventually degrade with the handle, but it does mean buying and disposing of AAA batteries every few months.

accessibility.note: Needs no charging dock or outlet, which can matter for travel or a bathroom without counter space, and a spent AAA battery is easier to replace on the road than finding a proprietary charger.

products.description: quip's other ADA-listed model runs on a single removable AAA battery instead of a built-in rechargeable pack, so there is no charging dock and no dead sealed battery forcing a full replacement, at the cost of buying and disposing of batteries every few months.

products.name: Goby Electric Toothbrush

economical.note: Goby's own site prices the toothbrush at $75 as a one-time purchase, or $60 upfront if the buyer joins the recurring $6 replacement-head plan.

health.note: The ADA record for Goby Electric Toothbrush that this page previously cited no longer resolves (the link loops back on itself), and a search for Goby in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search returned no result. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Goby' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Sold mainly direct-to-consumer through Goby's own site and Amazon rather than in physical stores, with a lower price tied to joining a recurring head subscription.

products.description: A direct-to-consumer sonic brush whose former ADA Seal record no longer turns up in the ADA's product search (checked 2026-10), sold either as a one-time purchase or at a lower upfront price tied to a recurring head subscription.

products.name: Bitvae Smart Electric Toothbrush

health.note: The ADA record for Bitvae Smart Electric Toothbrush, applicant Clevo Innovation Inc, that this page previously cited no longer resolves (the link loops back on itself), and a search for Bitvae in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search returned no result. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Bitvae' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Sold mainly through Amazon rather than through a brand site with clear direct pricing; the listing's own title advertises the ADA acceptance.

products.description: A budget sonic brush sold mainly through Amazon marketplace listings rather than a brand storefront, whose former ADA Seal record no longer turns up in the ADA's product search (checked 2026-10); a stable brand-site price could not be confirmed, so it is not scored on cost here.

products.name: Laifen Wave

economical.note: Laifen's own site prices the Wave at $69 for the ABS plastic handle, $79 for aluminum alloy, and $99 for stainless steel; replacement heads are $9.99 for a 3-pack.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Laifen' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Laifen Wave Electric Toothbrush' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed, one of the more recent additions to the ADA's list.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through Laifen's own site and Amazon, with an optional companion app; three handle materials at three price points give a buyer more choice than most other brands here.

products.description: A newer sonic-and-oscillating brush with its own ADA Seal record, priced by handle material: plastic, aluminum or steel.

products.name: BURST Sonic Toothbrush

economical.note: Burst's own site prices the Original Sonic Toothbrush at $69.99, with a recurring replacement-head plan at $7 every 12 weeks.

health.note: Burst's own site states of ADA status: 'Stay tuned for ADA acceptance!', meaning the brand itself says it does not currently hold the ADA Seal of Acceptance.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through Burst's own site on a subscription model for replacement heads, plus some third-party retail.

products.description: A subscription-model sonic brush; Burst's own site says it is not yet ADA-accepted.

products.name: SURI Pro 2.0

economical.note: SURI's own site prices the Pro 2.0 at $105 for the brush alone or $135 with the UV-C case.

health.note: No result for Suri appeared when searching the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product-search tool on the date checked; absence from a voluntary program is not the same as failing a test, and Suri sells mainly outside the US.

environment.note: SURI's own product page states the brush heads are made from cornstarch and castor oil and are 'fully recyclable' through the brand's free returns program, which is a stronger recycling claim than any other brand scored here.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through SURI's own site only, and at $105 to $135 it is the most expensive brush in this roster, which limits who can consider it.

ethics.note: B Lab's Certified B Corporation directory lists Coral Innovations Ltd, trading as SURI, as a Certified B Corp.

products.description: A UK-made brush from a Certified B Corporation, with brush heads the company recycles for free; it did not turn up in the ADA's product search on the date checked, and it is the most expensive brush in this roster.

products.name: Spotlight Oral Care Sonic Toothbrush

economical.note: Spotlight Oral Care's own EU site prices the Sonic Toothbrush at 69.99 euros.

health.note: The brand's own product page does not claim an ADA Seal of Acceptance or an Oral Health Foundation accreditation; it states only that the brush was 'designed by dentists.'

accessibility.note: Sold direct through Spotlight's own site and through UK retailers such as Superdrug, with up to 70 days of battery life between charges per the brand's own page.

products.description: A UK sonic brush; its own product page makes no claim to an ADA or Oral Health Foundation seal.

products.name: Waterpik Sonic-Fusion 2.0

economical.note: Waterpik's own store lists the Sonic-Fusion 2.0 at $179.99, on sale at $139.99 on the date checked.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Waterpik' as of the date checked. Separately, Waterpik's own product page states the Sonic-Fusion 2.0 'is accepted by the American Dental Association (ADA) for safety and effectiveness,' matching the ADA's own product-search record for 'Waterpik Sonic-Fusion Toothbrush/Flosser.'

accessibility.note: A combined sonic toothbrush and water flosser in one handle, sold through major retailers such as Best Buy and Walmart, but at $139.99 to $179.99 it is the highest price in this roster and is a different, bulkier device than a brush-only model.

products.description: A combined sonic toothbrush and water flosser in one handle, with its own ADA Seal record and the highest price in this roster.

products.name: AquaSonic Icon

economical.note: AquaSonic's own product page lists the Icon Rechargeable Power Toothbrush at $19.95 in every colour, shown as a sale from a regular price of $49.94, with a 1 year product warranty. Target's listing shows the same $19.95.

health.note: The ADA's product-search record for 'AquaSonic Icon Rechargeable Power Toothbrush', applicant AquaSonic of Los Angeles, states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs' acceptance is based on its finding that the product is 'safe and has shown efficacy in removing plaque' and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'AquaSonic' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Stocked by Target as well as sold direct, at $19.95 with a one-year limited warranty; Target's listing says the lithium-ion battery holds a charge for 30+ days of brushing, and sells AquaSonic's own Icon replacement heads at $9.95 for two.

products.description: A slim budget sonic brush with its own ADA Seal record, at about $20 from AquaSonic or Target, among the cheapest ADA-accepted rechargeables on this page.

products.name: Philips Sonicare 1100

economical.note: Target lists the Philips Sonicare 1100 (model HX3641/02) at a regular price of $19.99, with one C1 brush head and a USB charger (power adaptor not included).

health.note: No Philips Sonicare toothbrush appeared in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search on the date checked: a search for Sonicare returned only the Philips Sonicare Power Flosser, a water flosser, and a search for ProtectiveClean returned nothing. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Sonicare' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Stocked by Target at $19.99 with a 2-year limited warranty; the listing gives up to 14 days of brushing per charge and uses Philips' C1 Simply Clean replacement head, with a 2-minute timer and 30-second quadrant pacer.

products.description: Philips' cheapest sonic brush at about $20, with a USB charger and a two-week battery; no Sonicare toothbrush turned up in the ADA's product search in October 2026.

products.name: Philips Sonicare DiamondClean Smart 9300

economical.note: Target lists the Philips Sonicare DiamondClean Smart 9300 (HX9903/15) at $229.99, the highest handle price on this page.

health.note: No Philips Sonicare toothbrush appeared in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search on the date checked: a search for Sonicare returned only the Philips Sonicare Power Flosser, a water flosser. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Sonicare' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Stocked by Target with a charger base and a 2-year limited warranty, but at $229.99 it costs more than ten times Philips' own entry model, which limits who can consider it.

products.description: Philips' premium sonic brush, the most expensive handle on this page; no Sonicare toothbrush turned up in the ADA's product search in October 2026.

products.name: Colgate 360 Vibrate (AAA battery)

economical.note: Target lists the Colgate 360 Vibrate Deep Clean battery toothbrush at $7.99 for a pack of two complete brushes ($4.00 each), each with one AAA battery included.

health.note: No Colgate powered toothbrush appeared in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search on the date checked: a search for Colgate returned Colgate toothpastes and mouthwashes but no toothbrush. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Colgate' on the date checked.

environment.note: Target's listing sells it as a pack of complete brushes with a reminder to replace the toothbrush every three months, as with a manual brush, so the motor, battery compartment and handle go out with the bristles. The free toothbrush recycling programme Colgate sponsors through TerraCycle states: 'Electric toothbrushes, battery toothbrushes, and/or their parts are not accepted for recycling through the program.'

accessibility.note: Sold in grocery and big-box aisles such as Target's at $7.99 for two; it needs no charger, runs on one AAA battery, and the listing pitches it for travel for that reason.

products.description: A cheap vibrating brush that runs on one AAA battery and is thrown away whole when its bristles wear out; Colgate's own toothbrush recycling programme does not take battery brushes, and no Colgate powered brush turned up in the ADA's product search.

products.name: up&up Kids' Battery Powered Toothbrush

economical.note: Target lists its own-brand up&up Kids' Battery Powered Toothbrush at $3.99, with one AA battery included; a 2-pack of replacement heads is $6.99.

health.note: The ADA's product-search record for 'up&up Kids Battery Powered Toothbrush', applicant Target Corporation, lists the claims 'Helps remove plaque' and helps prevent and reduce gingivitis, and carries the label warning to use with adult supervision and not for children under three. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database showed no toothbrush among its recall records for 'Target' on the date checked.

environment.note: Target's listing gives a replaceable brush head and one AA alkaline battery rather than a sealed rechargeable pack, and makes a post-consumer recycled material claim; replacement heads are sold separately, so the handle can outlast several heads.

accessibility.note: Sold only at Target, where both the brush and its 2-pack of replacement heads are stocked; it needs no charger and is suggested for ages 4 and up.

products.description: Target's own-brand children's battery brush, the cheapest powered brush on this page, with its own ADA Seal record, a replaceable head and a standard AA battery.

products.name: up&up Kids Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush

economical.note: Target lists its own-brand up&up Kids Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush at $11.99, on sale from $13.99, with one handle, one charger and one brush head.

health.note: The ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search returns a record titled 'up&up Kids Rechargeable Toothbrush'; the record page itself showed only the product name on the date checked, and Target's listing names the ADA Seal of Acceptance among the product's certifications. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database showed no toothbrush among its recall records for 'Target' on the date checked.

environment.note: Target's listing specifies a non-universal lithium-ion battery that is non-removable, so when the battery wears out the whole handle is discarded, though the brush head is replaceable.

accessibility.note: Sold only at Target, with a two-minute quadrant timer and two modes, suggested for ages 4 and up; it needs its own charger.

products.description: Target's own-brand children's sonic rechargeable, listed in the ADA's product search, with a sealed battery that cannot be replaced.

products.name: Oral-B Kids' Electric Toothbrush

economical.note: Target lists the Oral-B Kids' Electric Toothbrush with Sensitive Brush Head and Timer at $24.99, with a charger base.

health.note: The ADA's record for Oral-B Oscillating-Rotating-Pulsating, applicant Procter & Gamble Co., names the models it covers (such as the Pro 500, Pro 1000, Smart and Genius lines) and none of them is a children's model; a search of the ADA product tool for kids returned no Oral-B brush. Absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Oral-B' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Stocked by Target with a 2-year limited warranty; it takes Oral-B's round-style heads (the listing gives an extra-soft round head) and is suggested for ages 3 and up.

products.description: Oral-B's rechargeable children's brush; Oral-B's ADA record names its adult Pro, Smart and Genius models but no children's model.

products.name: autobrush Sonic Pro (U-shaped)

economical.note: autobrush's own page lists the Sonic Pro at a regular price of $89, or $74 with a subscription; replacement brush heads start from $25 for a 2-month pack.

health.note: The ADA's product-search record for 'autobrush U-shaped Toothbrush Series', applicant Lander Enterprises LLC dba autobrush, states acceptance is based on the finding that the product is 'safe and has shown efficacy in removing plaque' and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed; autobrush's own page notes the acceptance covers its electric brushes and heads only. The CPSC check is not clean: the CPSC lists an April 2026 recall of the delivery boxes of autobrush's children's Sonic Pro Kids model, which held an easily reached lithium coin battery.

accessibility.note: Sold direct from autobrush's own site, built around a subscription for its U-shaped heads, which come in sizes from age 3 to adult XL; it is not a hands-free device and the page explains a specific side-to-side, figure-eight technique.

ethics.note: The CPSC's April 2026 recall notice covers about 48,000 Sonic Pro Kids delivery boxes sold from March 2023 to December 2025 that 'violate the mandatory standard for consumer products containing button cell and coin batteries' and lacked the warning labels Reese's Law requires; the remedy offered was a $5 refund in store credit. No injuries were reported.

products.description: A U-shaped mouthpiece brush with its own ADA Seal record; its maker recalled the packaging of its children's model in April 2026 for breaking the federal coin-battery safety standard.

products.name: Fairywill E11

economical.note: Fairywill's own US store lists the E11 Sonic Electric Toothbrush with 8 brush heads at $41.99.

health.note: A search for Fairywill in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search returned no result on the date checked; absence from a voluntary programme is not a failed test. Separately, the CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Fairywill' on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Sold online rather than in US stores; the bundle includes 8 heads, charges by USB (adapter not included) and the brand's page claims over 30 days per 2-hour charge. The one-year warranty charges an $8 restocking and shipping fee on claims it judges not related to product quality.

products.description: A low-cost online sonic brush sold with eight heads in the box; it did not turn up in the ADA's product search.

products.name: The Humble Co. bamboo toothbrush (manual)

economical.note: Target lists The Humble Co. Adult White Soft Toothbrush, a bamboo-handled manual brush, at $7.99 for one brush; Target also lists a 5-pack of the brand's plant-based plastic brush at $6.39.

health.note: A search for Humble in the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product search returned no Humble product on the date checked, so this brush has no ADA record of its own, although the ADA's general guidance is that manual and powered brushes both remove plaque when used properly. The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Humble' on the date checked.

environment.note: Target's listing says the handle is made from 100% bamboo with BPA-free nylon bristles, so there is no battery, motor or plastic handle to discard. Used manual toothbrushes of any brand are accepted by the free TerraCycle programme Colgate sponsors, which does not take powered brushes, though that programme warns enrollment limits may apply.

accessibility.note: Stocked by Target in the US, with no charger or replacement head to buy. The brand's own site, priced in pounds and euros, lists its bamboo brushes at £2.95 each but carries a notice that it is shipping 'A SMALLER RANGE, JUST FOR NOW' while it makes updates, so direct supply outside the US is patchy.

products.description: A bamboo-handled manual brush, the low-waste floor for comparison: no battery, no charger and no motor, though it has no ADA record of its own.
